content:
Independent Astra round2 acceptance review — experimental opt-in accepted; thorough optimization completion held

The frozen round2 candidate is acceptable for **experimental opt-in integration with existing defaults retained**. I found no remaining concrete correctness blocker in the reviewed supported paths. The previous workspace, transported identity, original-expiry and actual-opportunity-test findings are materially repaired. This is not approval to enable asynchronous opportunity scoring by default, qualify graphs/distributed layouts, or claim general ARC parity.

**The user's sustained background-cost investigation is not complete.** Readiness and readback still consume substantial executor thread CPU. A narrow host-wait experiment is an important unresolved lead, not a new capacity/admission campaign. Safe opt-in integration can proceed while that work remains explicitly open; “thoroughly optimized” cannot honestly be certified from this package.

I independently inspected the checkpoint, research criteria, prior diagnosis/rejection, full round2 report/protocol/source audit, final implementation, patches, CPU/tiny fixture code, frozen records, raw results/logs/traces and cleanup receipts. I used read-only source inspection and standard-library parsing/hashing on Mac. I ran no tests, model, GPU, PC, custody, install, settings or Git mutation and delegated nothing. Only this report was written. Test passes below are retained execution evidence, not tests rerun by this reviewer. Production source remains intentionally unchanged.

**Prior correctness findings and final acceptance evidence**

1. **Workspace bound: repaired for the implemented tensor expressions.** [worker.py:1098](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/worker.py:1098) validates `[requests, heads, dim]`, request count, real floating fields and exact head/dimension compatibility before admission. It charges unique backing storage of required summary fields, source-query backing, owned float32 query, two promoted field-stack envelopes, the batch-scaled products, cuboid endpoints, reductions/results and max-index allowance. I checked this against the actual expressions in [index.py:73](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/index.py:73) and the no-grad scoring body. Mean needs one full R×K×H×D product; minmax/cuboid conservatively reserve three, with cuboid endpoints separately charged. Promotion includes float32 query versus wider summary fields. Queue envelopes sum across admitted work, and full queues reject before bank scanning. The prior R16/K1024/H8/D128 counterexample is now rejected for all three methods by [test_round2.py:151](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/tests/test_round2.py:151). Shape rejection is separately tested. The tests do not exhaust dtype/layout combinations; the promoted-dtype conclusion is also a source-level argument. This remains a tensor job envelope, not a whole-process or allocator-reserved-memory ceiling: query bank, durable cache, Python result/transport objects, CUDA context and caching allocator are excluded as disclosed.

2. **Immutable residency and source identity reach the final consumer on both async routes.** [manager.py:710](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/manager.py:710) stamps every returned store admission, removes eviction entries and exports only ready current versions. [connector.py:5622](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/connector.py:5622) issues source tokens at request START, retains a time-limited normal-completion lease, invalidates abort/error, and combines a unique scheduler identity with its reset generation. Reset clears source state. [connector.py:8881](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/connector.py:8881) installs this context before score requests; [worker.py:1393](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/worker.py:1393) cancels changed source/epoch state before the next capture stride. [worker.py:1164](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/worker.py:1164) snapshots epoch, source tokens, residency versions and original expiry for continuous as well as opportunity work. [connector.py:9205](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/connector.py:9205) requires bounded-v2 in async configurations, rejects missing mandatory identity, compares current epoch/source/residency, and applies opportunity hint leases before updating relevance. This closes the previously identified publication-to-consumption hole, including same-key reinsertion and same-ID start before another sampled query.

   [test_round2.py:122](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/tests/test_round2.py:122) exercises native continuous delayed transport for reinsertion, START, abort, reset and duplicate delivery. The opportunity cases also cover invalid leases and reordered observations. Normal completion retains a final valid observation. The epoch-scoped sequence watermark rejects duplicates and earlier reordered observations conservatively; it is not a replay buffer and does not promise exactly-once history or synchronous EMA equivalence. Advancing it before all per-source filters can discard an earlier otherwise-valid observation after a later unusable one; that is consistent with the declared conservative drop semantics, not stale-score acceptance.

3. **Original feature expiry: repaired.** Submission uses capture time plus `min(query_age, async_age)` for opportunity; continuous uses async age. Publication and final consumption retain that deadline. [test_round2.py:141](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/tests/test_round2.py:141) uses the requested unequal 100 ms/1000 ms case and delayed publication. Re-scoring or normal completion does not refresh the feature timestamp.

4. **Actual opportunity integration: the new test closes the earlier gap.** [test_round2.py:27](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/tests/test_round2.py:27) constructs the real scheduler, ARC manager, Request, BlockPool, connector-worker and semantic worker. `compete()` enters opportunity mode, creates two positively eligible sources with 32 ready blocks competing for 16 staging slots, builds scheduler requests, binds native metadata, computes actual tensor scores and passes worker metadata to the real consumer. [test_round2.py:71](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/tests/test_round2.py:71) asserts warm-a's exact 16-key prefix wins, duplicate delivery leaves EMA unchanged, and ARC remains the policy. [test_round2.py:111](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/tests/test_round2.py:111) verifies pending at 49 ms and explicit unscored dispatch at 51 ms. Original timestamps and ordered EMA/reference composition are checked separately.

   The seams are material and accurately bounded: the CUDA transfer-handler constructor is stubbed; the connector role facade uses `__new__`; model queries and durable summaries are supplied tensors. These tests establish scheduler/metadata/score/consumer correctness, not actual model query capture or CUDA transfer execution. Earlier helper tests still use broader stubs and are not substitutes for this new coverage. [CPU.py](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/CPU.py) guards CUDA initialization; the retained [CPU execution receipt](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/evidence/cpu-final.activity.json) records 363 passing tests.

5. **Ownership/failure handling: adequate for this opt-in, with a fixture limitation.** [worker.py:1030](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/worker.py:1030) retains payload references through blocking result readback and synchronizes the scoring stream on partial-enqueue exceptions before allowing the failed job to release its charge. Normal polling drains only a ready ordered prefix; ordinary completion does not wait for unrelated work; reset/shutdown deliberately drain. [tiny.py:29](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/tiny.py:29) uses real CUDA producer events, a gated reader, source overwrite, removal of durable-summary references, poison allocations, an injected exception after actual enqueue and exact recovery scores of 2 and 12. The retained tiny result reports success and 48,128 allocated bytes, excluding context setup.

   **Do not overstate “allocation recycling” or adversarial failure coverage.** At tiny.py:42 the original query is overwritten but its local reference is not deleted; poison allocations do not assert reuse of a particular freed address. The short device sleep may complete while the Python failure gate is held; `done.query()` after drain does not prove that device work was still pending immediately before the exception. These are useful ownership/pressure checks plus source evidence, not a deterministic proof against every premature-release mutation. This is a nonblocking evidence limitation for unchanged current fences. If readback/fencing changes, strengthen the tiny gate to demonstrate genuinely outstanding device work at failure and prevent payload/buffer reuse until completion. No model run is needed for that gate.

**Artifact identity and independent numerical checks**

I rehashed all 196 round2 manifest members (13,802,171 bytes), all 56 final pin entries, and all 340 preserved round1 manifest members: no mismatches. Both fullpatch-versus-baseline and round1delta were applied **in memory**, checking exact hunk context; each reconstructed all 55 final Python files byte-for-byte. Authoritative pins are [final candidate pins](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/evidence/candidate-pins.json), not the inherited candidate/candidate-pins.json. The frozen source/hooks/driver pins match the delivered files; run.py:160 verifies these before each arm, and all five raw configurations match the freeze. This establishes source/evidence consistency, not independent reproduction of execution.

Round2's diagnostic and products use the same frozen candidate source; they intentionally differ in schedule/stride and observers (continuous stride1 diagnostic versus opportunity stride8 products). The historical round1 diagnostic predates its final retirement/nonfinite/status changes and the round2 repairs. Its corrected trace supports the earlier capture mechanism, not a final-source performance estimate. The reconstructed runtime/wheel and metadata-based cached-weight provenance remain limitations; no new full weight-content hash or original-runtime byte identity is claimed.

I independently compared all five runs with the preserved prior ARC anchor: 225 successful requests, 16,320 exact output tokens, exact prompts and ordered native keys, and 30,345 rehashed block-key recurrences. Recorded transfer jobs succeeded. In both final product arms I additionally checked selected ordered prefixes, staging destination mappings, transfer completion before readiness/splice, splice acknowledgement/cleanup, and recorded CUDA/default-stream fence evidence. Each consumed seven blocks, all through transfer-plus-splice fallback; native adoption was zero. These are checks of retained observations and code, not a new hardware experiment.

Recomputed whole-load throughput and intended-release TTFT reproduce [paired comparisons](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/evidence/comparisons.json):

| Frozen pair | Throughput change | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Background mean TTFT | Screen |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| new1 / arc1 | +0.311% | −0.125% | −0.002% | −0.251% | Pass |
| new2 / arc2 | +0.396% | −0.417% | −0.511% | −0.573% | Pass |

Both meet the predeclared within-1% throughput and no-more-than-5%-worse selected-TTFT screen. This is a practical result for two reversed pairs on this small Qwen3-4B BF16 TP1 eager closed-loop workload, **not statistical equivalence, a causal speedup, broad throughput parity or ranking utility**. All arms complete 45 requests/3,264 output tokens. Executed prompt work differs by 32 tokens (80,531 final versus 80,499 ARC), and completion-dependent releases feed back into scheduling. No p95 or SLO improvement follows from these samples. Product component/runtime profile files are absent as declared; compact capture/key/terminal counters and operational events remain.

Both final products have 143 real capture batches/411 rows across lifecycle, including one warmup batch, and **zero async scoring jobs/competitive nominations**. The continuous diagnostic submits and publishes 1,030 actual jobs with 11 explicit full-queue pre-capture drops. CPU competition plus continuous CUDA scoring is useful complementary coverage; neither turns the product screen into a measured competitive-ranking benefit. Preserve the failed round1 matrix and rejection as negative evidence for its actual revision. Round2 legitimately supersedes acceptance for repaired source, not the historical result.

**Confirmed work reduction and overlap, with attribution limits**

The source removes empty-retirement waits, disabled-debug formatting, capture-disabled dispatch/layout work, repeated operator-name conversion, and continuous empty-bank extraction while preserving cadence. Required-field projection and selected publication fences reduce retained inputs and unnecessary dependencies. Owned slice/concatenation capture removes the old device-index construction path. Those changes are concrete; their individual end-to-end latency contributions were not isolated.

I independently recomputed host-category-only raw trace windows: round1 old/new have 12 host steps, envelopes 386.252/376.928 ms, recorded GPU unions 338.249/338.907 ms and cross-stream overlap 0.00634/0.37328 ms. GPU annotation tails no longer count as host executions. The earlier capture synchronization removal and real short-window overlap survive the correction. The final-source diagnostic includes actual first-summary/store plus 16 host steps: 607.494 ms envelope, 480.296 ms GPU union, 127.198 ms without recorded activity and 0.31184 ms cross-stream overlap. These totals are not exclusive scoring cost or recoverable latency.

[summary correlation evidence](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/evidence/summary-attribution.json) correctly distinguishes a 45.268 ms first-summary host span from 0.06935 ms of 50 correlated kernels and a 0.516 ms nested stream synchronization. One full KV D2H transfers 2,359,296 bytes in 44.321 microseconds; the other small readbacks are not additional full KV stores. Observed summary/D2H device overlap is zero, consistent with the retained serialized dependency. First-use observer/host overhead prevents treating 45 ms as DMA or removable compute. No source-block lifetime fence should be removed on this evidence.

Final product logs contain one idle-status record each, versus 1,141/1,178 in historical candidate products; duplicate JSON/flush work is demonstrably removed, but its latency effect is not isolated from other changes. Transfer totals also preclude claiming universally reduced traffic: final demand H2D falls, but speculative transfers and splice copies add movement. D2H copies do not themselves prove immediate GPU reuse. Fixed KV pool size, startup-inclusive allocation peaks and sampled occupancy support **no reduced-VRAM or capacity-gain claim**.

**Outstanding acceptance finding: background CPU cost remains consequential**

[async_scoring.py:128](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/async_scoring.py:128) synchronizes readiness fences in the executor; [worker.py:1160](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/worker.py:1160) creates a readiness event without an explicit blocking flag, and [worker.py:1067](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/worker.py:1067) uses CUDA `combined.tolist()`. Raw exported component aggregates reproduce:

| Scope | Calls | Host wall | Thread CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Readiness wait | 1,013 | 11.373 s | 11.332 s |
| Readback | 1,013 | 5.822 s | 5.806 s |
| Executor total, excluding readiness | 1,013 | 7.731 s | 6.786 s |

Near-equal wall/CPU in these waits is strong evidence consistent with substantial active host waiting. It does not prove the exact driver cause or the benefit of a particular replacement. The 17 trace-window jobs lack aggregate executor/thread-CPU scopes because [audit_trace.py:23](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/hooks/audit_trace.py:23) substitutes record_function; queue-wait count 1,030 is complete. Whole-lifecycle scopes can include startup. CUDA event ranges contain ordering/launch gaps. Inclusive readback and executor totals must not be added; thread-CPU endpoints include profiler bookkeeping after wall sampling ([profiling.py:70](/Users/pippo/github/vllm-semantic-cache-ext/output/scoring-audit/round2-results/round2/candidate/semantic_offload/profiling.py:70)), biasing very short scopes. The 8.893 ms wall versus 10.212 ms CPU rank anomaly is therefore disclosed and plausible observer bias, not a performance miracle.

Moving this cost off the launch callback is valuable, but **overlap does not eliminate CPU consumption or contention with other work**. The zero-job products cannot evaluate this residual cost. I reject dismissing it solely because foreground throughput passes.

The smallest useful next work is:

- Check the installed runtime's event host-wait behavior, then compare the current readiness event against a `blocking=True` event with otherwise identical producer/consumer dependencies. This is a hypothesis to test, not an established fix. Scope it to owned host-wait readiness events; retain source/summary dependencies, cancellation and failure fences. It requires no new subsystem or buffers.
- If readback CPU remains material, compare a bounded per-job pinned result copy plus a blocking completion wait against current `tolist()`. Read CPU results only after copy completion; charge and retain the host destination and GPU result through success, cancellation and failure. Reuse only within the existing queue/byte limits; no independent unbounded queue or buffer pool. This second step has more ownership complexity than the event flag and should be conditional on measured benefit.
- Use a tiny real-device comparison first: identical scores/ties, deliberate delayed producer/reader, partial enqueue failure, budget recovery, pending-work checks, per-thread CPU and wall latency. Capture all compared jobs without replacing aggregate scopes during tracing, and sample both end timestamps before metric aggregation. Report observer overhead and completion/drop/expiry effects. Reject a change that trades useful latency/freshness for CPU savings without making that tradeoff explicit.

This is within the user's stated scoring/background-cost objective. It is not authority for this reviewer to launch anything, resume a paused owner, or enlarge the GPU budget. The current checkpoint says no more GPU work after the fixed block; any followup must first be explicitly reconciled by the owning parent with existing resource controls. No new admission, threshold, capacity or organic-competition campaign is required for this narrow question. A model comparison is not the first gate, and the current frozen product result must remain attached to its current source if a later change is made.

Other leads remain measured only partially: repeated async stack construction, metadata/context scanning and serialization, duplicate snapshot copies, and mean-mode construction of unused min/max/MAD fields. The shared exported summary schema and other methods make the latter more involved than deleting a reduction. One tiny summary trace and an 11-block stored pool do not justify fusion, an index, CPU mirrors or a new stack-cache subsystem now. Deferral is reasonable; claiming those avenues experimentally exhausted is not.

**Integration and handback gates**

Proceed with the exact pinned implementation as experimental opt-in, retain current defaults and supported-layout restrictions, and preserve original-expiry, identity, sequence, residency and buffer-lifetime gates. Keep the frozen tests/evidence and failed round1 results linked. Do not substitute broad safety/performance language for the specific TP1 dense eager qualification. No correctness repair or new model run is required by this review before that limited integration.

Keep the background-CPU finding open before declaring the sustained optimization objective complete. The event-wait experiment is the first targeted remaining gate; the pinned readback alternative is conditional, not a requirement to add complexity regardless of outcome. Broad parity/default promotion and ranking-utility claims remain unapproved.

The separate cleanup HANDOFF and receipts disclose quiet-custody expiry after GPU work, a rejected later CPU launch, sealed restoration/reconciliation, and a fresh CPU-only patch-validation session. Final receipts record restored protected pins, empty owned process trees, a free project lock, released custody and removal of obsolete own waits. I inspected those records without contacting the PC or changing ownership. This review created no disposable execution artifacts or persistent processes; only this useful report remains.
